title: Jersey City Rent Control allowable rent increase cap
requirement: A landlord may not increase rent by more than 4% or the CPI change over the lease term, whichever is less, only once in any 12-month period. Vacant-unit rent may exceed that only for registered capital improvements at set rates.
key_value: 4% or CPI increase, whichever is less
coverage_conditions: All dwellings in Jersey City with five or more housing spaces; owner-occupied dwellings with four or fewer spaces, hotels and motels, commercial space, certain redevelopment housing, low-rent public housing and post-October 1983 conversions are exempt.

conditions.text: newly constructed dwellings with 25 or more units in a city-approved redevelopment area
buildings converted from nonpermanent dwelling use to dwelling use on or after October 1, 1983

applicability.per_tenancy: New dwellings or housing spaces rented for the first time are exempt for the initial rental only.
coverage_quotes: Dwellings with four or less housing spaces; provided, however, that this exemption shall be suspended for non-owner occupied dwellings with four or less housing spaces until the end of the state of emergency or six months from adoption of these amendments whichever comes first.

Newly constructed dwellings with 25 or more dwelling units located within a redevelopment area as defined in Section 5 of the Redevelopment Agencies Law, N.J.S.A. 40:55C-5(o), for which the City Council has approved a redevelopment plan, in accordance with Section 17 of the Redevelopment Agencies Law, N.J.S.A. 40:55C-17.
All buildings or structures, hotels, motels or guesthouses which are converted from any previous use as a nonpermanent dwelling to use as a dwelling on or after October 1, 1983.

exemptions: Dwellings with four or fewer housing spaces; licensed hotels and motels; commercial and industrial space; new redevelopment dwellings of 25 or more units; low-rent public housing; buildings converted to dwelling use on or after October 1, 1983; first rental of a new dwelling.
penalty: Any increase above the authorized amount is void, and the excess rent must be refunded or credited to the tenant forthwith.
quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of a lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord of any dwelling as defined in § 260-1 may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than four percent or the percentage difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less.
